newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech crown firms then steadies after budget vote.
newsitem.headline: Czech crown firms then steadies after budget vote.

text.p: The Czech crown was holding on to strong morning gains against its mark/dollar basket at midday on Thursday after the parliament passed the first reading of a balanced 1997 budget late on Wednesday evening.
The crown was trading 2.60 percent above parity with the basket at 1224 local time (1024 GMT) from Wednesday's Czech National Bank (CNB) fixing of 2.29 percent above the basket.

The market rate rose to even with the CNB's fixing in anticipation of the trend on Thursday. The CNB's fixing was calculated at a crown/dollar rate of 27.137 and a crown/mark rate of 17.720, also +2.60 against the basket.

"Immediately this morning, there was some stronger buying of the crown, especially against the mark and there's good support for the crown at this moment," said Tomas Becvar of Komercni Banka at mid-day on Thursday.
Becvar said he anticipated range trading between 2.6 percent and 2.7 percent above the mid-point but did not exclude the possibility the crown could rise to 2.8 percent.
The passing of the budget was no foregone conclusion and required the last minute defection of four opposition deputies to support the minority government.
In the run-up to the vote, the crown had weakened to less than two percent above the basket mid-point from highs of over four percent in early September.
